title: Centralize Redux Store Across Client Packages

questions.prompt: How should `davinci()`/`journey()` expose the store to consumers?
questions.description: The store is currently fully private. The simplest approach is adding a `store` property to the returned client object. An alternative is a dedicated `getStore()` method. A third option is exposing only an opaque handle typed as `SdkStore` (not the full Redux `Store` type) to discourage direct Redux usage.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Add a `store` property typed as an opaque `SdkStore` handle on the return object — additive, zero breaking changes, consumers can pass it to oidc() but can't easily misuse the raw Redux API.

questions.prompt: How should `oidc()` accept the shared store?
questions.description: Option A: add an optional `store` param to the existing config object — `oidc({ config, store: client.store })`. Option B: add it as a second argument — `oidc({ config }, client.store)`. The survey shows oidc() already takes a single destructured options bag.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Optional `store` field inside the existing options object — consistent with how requestMiddleware and logger are passed today.

options.label: Optional field in existing options object

questions.prompt: Should `wellknownApi` be deduplicated as part of this work?
questions.description: All three packages each define their own `wellknownApi` RTK Query slice with the same reducerPath ('wellknown') and endpoint. With a shared store, both registrations would collide on the same reducer key. We could: (A) keep them separate and let RTK Query's cache dedup on-the-fly (they share the same reducerPath so this actually works), (B) extract `wellknownApi` to `sdk-effects` so both packages import the same instance, or (C) defer this to a follow-up.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Extract wellknownApi to sdk-effects as part of this PR — the same-key collision is a latent bug we'd hit immediately when testing shared store, and extraction is straightforward.

options.label: Extract wellknownApi to sdk-effects in this PR
Rely on RTK Query same-key dedup (same reducerPath)

questions.prompt: How should oidc inject its reducers into a shared store?
questions.description: RTK 2.0 ships `combineSlices` and lazy reducer injection. Two clean approaches: (A) use `store.dispatch(oidcApi.util.updateSubscriptionOptions(...))` + manually add reducer via `store.injectReducers` if RTK exposes it, or (B) design `createClientStore` / `createJourneyStore` to pre-register all possible reducers with their slices (oidc's included) so the store is fully wired before oidc() receives it. Option B is simpler but slightly over-provisions; Option A is lazy but requires RTK 2.0 `combineSlices`.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Pre-register all reducers in the owning store (davinci/journey) — avoids runtime injection complexity, reducer keys don't collide (config/node/davinci/journeyReducer/oidc/wellknown are all unique), and the extra state is negligible.

options.label: Pre-register oidc reducers in davinci/journey store upfront
Lazy inject via RTK combineSlices at oidc() init time

questions.prompt: Which packages are in scope for this change?
questions.description: davinci-client and journey-client are the store owners; oidc-client is the joiner. protect and device-client don't use Redux stores currently.

Exposing `store` on the return object is purely additive. Adding `store?` to oidc's options bag is additive. The only potential breaking change is if `wellknownApi` is extracted to sdk-effects and packages previously imported it directly — but that's an internal import path change, not a public API change.
questions.recommendedAnswer: No breaking changes to public API — internal import path changes are acceptable.
